title: 02 Renaissance

blocks.text: Renaissance brought humanism, printing, and golden-age polyphony — Palestrina, Josquin, Byrd.
Independent vocal lines woven in imitative counterpoint. Mass settings and madrigals. Consonance rules refined; dissonance on weak beats.
Lute flourished; viol consort; early keyboard. Dance music published in collections (Attaignant, Praetorius).
Lutheran chorales and Anglican hymnody shaped congregational singing — ancestors of folk hymn tradition.

- A) Imitative vocal polyphony
- B) Heavy distortion guitar
- C) 4/4 rock backbeat only
- D) Serial twelve-tone rows

**Answer:** A

sections.title: Q2. Music printing spread repertoire widely in the Renaissance.

quiz_markdown:
### Q1. Renaissance music emphasises:

- A) Imitative vocal polyphony
- B) Heavy distortion guitar
- C) 4/4 rock backbeat only
- D) Serial twelve-tone rows

**Answer:** A

### Q2. Music printing spread repertoire widely in the Renaissance.

**Answer:** True
